items.title: Most Fed policymakers see hike before year-end
items.summary: WASHINGON, D.C. — US Federal Reserve minutes released on Wednesday show most policymakers foresee another interest rate hike by year’s end, as the central bank targets stubbornly high inflation.

items.title: US stocks: US markets fall as higher yields and oil prices flag inflation risk
items.summary: US stocks fell as crude oil prices surged and Treasury yields remained high, raising inflation concerns. Major companies like Amazon, Tesla, and Nvidia experienced losses, contributing to a broader decline in the technology sector. Investors are now focused on upcoming third-quarter earnings reports, particularly from financial institutions. The Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates unchanged in October, while considering future hikes.

items.title: Inflation Fears Surge Again: Americans' One-Year Outlook Hits Highest Level in More Than Three Years
items.summary: Median inflation expectations for the next 12 months jumped to 3.9%, up from 3.6% in August, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's September Survey of Consumer Expectations.

items.title: Global Market: European stocks slide as oil surge revives inflation concerns
items.summary: European shares fell as banks hit over three-month lows amid rising bond yields and oil prices. Investors worried persistent inflation could constrain central bank rate cuts and hurt growth, while markets awaited ECB, Federal Reserve and Bank of England signals.

items.title: Fed’s Waller Says There Is Some Flexibility on Rate-Hike Timing
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said further interest-rate hikes will likely be needed to slow inflation, though officials have some flexibility on timing and don’t need to tighten at consecutive policy meetings.

items.title: Fed policymakers divided over September rate
items.summary: US Federal Reserve policymakers were divided last month over the rationale for raising interest rates, with "some participants" seeing a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay.

items.title: Dollar edges back from 18-month high after FOMC minutes
items.summary: The dollar index has maintained its position as hawkish Fed minutes emphasize inflation as a major concern. Recent interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve have been met with caution regarding future increases. Meanwhile, the US dollar's performance varied against other currencies, influenced by Japan's positive current account surplus report.

items.title: Dollar edges back from 18-month high after FOMC minutes
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The dollar held near its strongest level in a year-and-a-half in subdued trading at the start of the Asian session on Thursday, after hawkish minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee signaled policymakers at the US central bank viewed inflation as the biggest risk to their outlook.

items.title: Ticker: Fed minutes: Another rate hike likely
items.summary: Most Federal Reserve officials expect that another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year to combat inflation, according to minutes released Wednesday from the central bank's most recent meeting.
